eligible.content: I'll keep that in mind—maybe I'll check a couple more pots tomorrow before watering again. It's just tricky when the heat makes everything feel so dry on the surface.

Sounds like a smart approach! Monitoring the soil moisture directly is a good idea. Just remember to check the top layer first—if it still feels dry, that's your cue to water. Good luck with the monitoring! Let me know how it goes!

sources.content: I'll try moving them to the east side where they get morning sun but not the harsh afternoon heat. Let me check if the pots are heavy—some of them are pretty full.

That sounds like a solid plan! Moving them to the east side sounds like a great way to keep them out of that intense afternoon heat.

Since you mentioned the pots are pretty heavy, are they in heavy ceramic pots, or is it just that the soil is dense and packed tight? That might affect how fast the water drains out, which is important for the health of the roots.
I think they're just heavy because the soil is packed tight—most of them are plastic. I'll try to water them more thoroughly this time, but I'm worried about overwatering in the heat.

It sounds like the soil is holding a lot of moisture right now, which is common with plastic pots. If you're worried about overwatering, try to monitor the soil moisture before watering them again—maybe just a gentle touch or a quick "squeeze test" on the top inch or so of soil to see if it still feels slightly damp. Better to be a bit on the light side than to have roots get waterlogged, which can cause rot!
